task: Hide the "Register Now" button on the conference detail page for COMPLETED and CANCELLED conferences while keeping it visible and functional for UPCOMING and ACTIVE/ONGOING ones.

key_reasoning.reason: Core AC are four crisp checkboxes, but three decisions are open: which value set counts as "active" (ACTIVE is seeded in DataInitializer, ONGOING is the documented allowableValue, and the two ConferenceListPage dropdowns disagree); the null-status policy (status is a nullable unvalidated String, and the only precedent — the getStatusBadgeClass helpers — treats null as upcoming); and hide-vs-disable, since the DoD says "not visible" while ConferenceDetailPage.jsx:372 only sets disabled. Each is small and pre-diagnosed in docs/tech-debt-audit.md FE-003, so M rather than L.

Base risk is S — the correct idiom already exists in-repo in two copies of getStatusBadgeClass (normalise with toLowerCase, then compare), the change is one JSX predicate, and rollback is trivial. Bumped to M because the AC enumerate specific status variants (completed, cancelled, upcoming, active) and the frontend has zero test infrastructure — no runner, no assertion library, no test script, no test files — so no existing test template covers the defensive variant matrix these AC describe. Secondary risk: RegistrationService.registerAttendee has no status guard and returns 201 for COMPLETED/CANCELLED, so the UI remains the only defence and the unlinked-but-reachable /conferences/:id/register route stays open.

One component — ConferenceDetailPage.jsx — carries the only register affordance in the app, and conference.status is already fetched and already rendered twice. RegistrationPage.jsx is an optional second component only if the unlinked standalone route is brought in scope.

red_flags_applied: Technical Risk bumped from S to M: acceptance criteria enumerate specific status variants (completed/cancelled/upcoming/active) and no existing test template covers that defensive pattern — the frontend has no test runner, no assertion library and no test files at all.
